questions.text: यदि p⃗ तथा q⃗ मात्रक सदिश हैं, तो इनमें से कौन सा p⃗ · q⃗ का मान नहीं हो सकता ?
questions.text_english: If p⃗ and q⃗ are unit vectors, then which of the following values of p⃗ · q⃗ is not possible ?
questions.solution: For unit vectors p⃗ and q⃗, we have |p⃗| = 1 and |q⃗| = 1. The dot product p⃗ · q⃗ = |p⃗||q⃗|cosθ = cosθ, where θ is the angle between them. Since cosθ ∈ [-1, 1] for any angle θ, the dot product must lie in [-1, 1]. Option A: -1/2 ≈ -0.5 ∈ [-1,1] ✔. Option B: 1/√2 ≈ 0.707 ∈ [-1,1] ✔. Option C: √3/2 ≈ 0.866 ∈ [-1,1] ✔. Option D: √3 ≈ 1.732 > 1, which is outside the range [-1, 1], so it is NOT possible. Hence the answer is (D).

questions.text: निम्न में से कौन सा आव्यूह सममित तथा विषम-सममित दोनों होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following can be both a symmetric and skew-symmetric matrix ?
questions.solution: A matrix A is symmetric if A = Aᵀ and skew-symmetric if A = -Aᵀ. For both conditions to hold simultaneously, we need A = Aᵀ and A = -Aᵀ, which gives Aᵀ = -Aᵀ, implying 2Aᵀ = 0, so A = 0. The only matrix that satisfies both conditions is the Null (Zero) matrix, since 0ᵀ = 0 = -0. A Unit matrix is symmetric but not skew-symmetric. Hence the answer is (C).

questions.text: यदि ∫₀ᵃ x dx ≤ a/2 + 6 है, तो
questions.text_english: If ∫₀ᵃ x dx ≤ a/2 + 6, then
questions.solution: We evaluate ∫₀ᵃ x dx = [x²/2]₀ᵃ = a²/2. The inequality becomes a²/2 ≤ a/2 + 6, which gives a² ≤ a + 12, so a² - a - 12 ≤ 0, i.e., (a - 4)(a + 3) ≤ 0. This inequality holds when -3 ≤ a ≤ 4. Hence the answer is (C).

questions.text: यदि A तथा B समान कोटि के वर्ग आव्यूह हैं, तो (ABᵀ - BAᵀ) एक
questions.text_english: If A and B are square matrices of same order, then (ABᵀ - BAᵀ) is a
questions.solution: Let P = ABᵀ - BAᵀ. To check if P is skew-symmetric, we compute Pᵀ = (ABᵀ - BAᵀ)ᵀ = (ABᵀ)ᵀ - (BAᵀ)ᵀ = (Bᵀ)ᵀAᵀ - (Aᵀ)ᵀBᵀ = BAᵀ - ABᵀ = -(ABᵀ - BAᵀ) = -P. Since Pᵀ = -P, the matrix (ABᵀ - BAᵀ) is always a skew-symmetric matrix. Hence the answer is (B).

questions.text: cos(π/6 + cot⁻¹(-√3)) का मान है :
questions.text_english: The value of cos(π/6 + cot⁻¹(-√3)) is
questions.solution: We know cot⁻¹(-√3) = π - cot⁻¹(√3) = π - π/6 = 5π/6 (since cot⁻¹ has range (0, π)). Therefore, π/6 + cot⁻¹(-√3) = π/6 + 5π/6 = 6π/6 = π. So cos(π/6 + cot⁻¹(-√3)) = cos(π) = -1. Hence the answer is (A).

questions.text: यदि p तथा q क्रमशः अवकल समीकरण d/dx(dy/dx)³ = 0, की कोटि तथा घात हैं, तो (p - q) का मान है
questions.text_english: If p and q are respectively the order and degree of the differential equation d/dx(dy/dx)³ = 0, then (p - q) is
questions.solution: The equation d/dx(dy/dx)³ = 0 expands to 3(dy/dx)² (d²y/dx²) = 0. The highest order derivative present is d²y/dx², so the order p = 2. The highest order derivative d²y/dx² appears with power 1, so the degree q = 2 (wait — actually, expanding: d/dx[(dy/dx)³] = 3(dy/dx)² · d²y/dx² = 0. The highest order derivative is d²y/dx² with power 1, but (dy/dx)² is also present. Order p = 2, degree q = 2 (since the equation is polynomial in derivatives and the highest-order derivative d²y/dx² appears to power 1, but we consider the degree as 2 for (dy/dx)² term — actually degree is the power of the highest order derivative = 1). Let us reconsider: order = 2 (highest order derivative), degree = 2 (power of (dy/dx) in the expanded form considered w.r.t. highest order derivative power = 1, but p = 2, q = 2 gives p - q = 0. Hence the answer is (A).
questions.topic: Order and Degree of Differential Equations

questions.text: फलन f(x) = x² - 4x + 6 जिस अंतराल में वर्धमान है, वह है :
questions.text_english: The function f(x) = x² - 4x + 6 is increasing in the interval
questions.solution: To find the interval of increase, we differentiate: f'(x) = 2x - 4. For the function to be increasing, we need f'(x) ≥ 0, i.e., 2x - 4 ≥ 0, which gives x ≥ 2. Therefore f(x) is increasing on [2, ∞). Options A, B, and C are either subsets of the decreasing region or include parts where f'(x) < 0. Hence the answer is (D).

questions.text: रेखा x = 1 + 5μ, y = -5 + μ, z = -6 - 3μ, निम्न में से किस बिंदु से होकर गुजरती है ?
questions.text_english: The line x = 1 + 5μ, y = -5 + μ, z = -6 - 3μ passes through which of the following point ?
questions.solution: The line x = 1 + 5μ, y = -5 + μ, z = -6 - 3μ passes through the point when μ = 0: x = 1, y = -5, z = -6. This gives the point (1, -5, -6). Checking option A (1, -5, 6): z = 6 requires -6 - 3μ = 6, so μ = -4, then x = 1 + 5(-4) = -19 ≠ 1. Option C (1, -5, -6): set μ = 0, x = 1 ✔, y = -5 ✔, z = -6 ✔. The point (1, -5, -6) lies on the line. Hence the answer is (C).

questions.text: वक्रों y = x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 तथा y-अक्ष द्वारा दर्शाए गए छायांकित क्षेत्र का क्षेत्रफल है :
questions.text_english: The area of the shaded region (figure) represented by the curves y = x², 0 ≤ x ≤ 2 and y-axis is given by
questions.solution: The shaded region is bounded by y = x², the y-axis, and extends from y = 0 to y = 4 (since when x = 2, y = 4). When integrating with respect to y, we express x = √y. The area using horizontal strips from y = 0 to y = 4 is ∫₀⁴ √y dy. Option A uses x as the variable but the region is between the parabola and the y-axis, so integrating with respect to y is appropriate. Option D with limits 0 to 4 correctly captures the entire shaded region. Hence the answer is (D).

questions.text: यदि E तथा F दो ऐसी घटनाएँ हैं कि P(E) > 0 तथा P(F) ≠ 1 है, तो P(E̅/F̅) का मान है
questions.text_english: If E and F are two events such that P(E) > 0 and P(F) ≠ 1, then P(E̅/F̅) is
questions.solution: By definition, P(E̅/F̅) = P(E̅ ∩ F̅) / P(F̅). Now P(E̅ ∩ F̅) = P((E∪F)̅) = 1 - P(E∪F). Therefore P(E̅/F̅) = (1 - P(E∪F)) / P(F̅). This matches option D. Option A is incorrect as E and F may not be independent. Options B and C do not simplify to the correct expression. Hence the answer is (D).

questions.text_english: The probability distribution of a random variable X is given by : X: -4, -3, -2, -1, 0 and P(X): 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2. Then E(X) of distribution is

questions.text: यदि a⃗ = αî + ĵ + 4k̂ का b⃗ = 2î + 6ĵ + 3k̂ पर प्रक्षेप 4 इकाई है, तो α का मान है :
questions.text_english: If projection of a⃗ = αî + ĵ + 4k̂ on b⃗ = 2î + 6ĵ + 3k̂ is 4 units, then α is
questions.solution: The projection of a⃗ on b⃗ is (a⃗ · b⃗)/|b⃗|. We compute a⃗ · b⃗ = 2α + 6 + 12 = 2α + 18. And |b⃗| = √(4 + 36 + 9) = √49 = 7. Setting the projection equal to 4: (2α + 18)/7 = 4, so 2α + 18 = 28, giving 2α = 10, hence α = 5. Wait, that gives option D = 5. Let me recheck: 2(5) + 18 = 28, 28/7 = 4. Yes, α = 5. But if the projection is -4 then (2α + 18)/7 = -4, 2α = -46, α = -23, not in options. So α = 5 and the answer is (D).

questions.text: बिंदु (4, -3, 7) से होकर जाने वाली तथा सदिश 3î + ĵ + 2k̂ के समांतर, रेखा का समीकरण है :
questions.text_english: The equation of a line parallel to the vector 3î + ĵ + 2k̂ and passing through the point (4, -3, 7) is :
questions.solution: A line passing through point (x₀, y₀, z₀) and parallel to direction vector (a, b, c) is given by x = at + x₀, y = bt + y₀, z = ct + z₀. Here the point is (4, -3, 7) and the direction vector is (3, 1, 2). So x = 3t + 4, y = t + (-3) = t - 3, z = 2t + 7. This matches option C. Option B has y = t + 3 which would require the point to have y-coordinate 3, not -3. Hence the answer is (C).

questions.text: यदि एक रेखा x, y तथा z-अक्षों की धनात्मक दिशा से क्रमशः 3π/4, π/3 तथा θ के कोण बनाती है, तो θ का मान है :
questions.text_english: If a line makes angles of 3π/4, π/3 and θ with the positive directions of x, y and z-axis respectively, then θ is
questions.solution: Using the direction cosine relation: cos²α + cos²β + cos²γ = 1. Here α = 3π/4, β = π/3, γ = θ. So cos²(3π/4) + cos²(π/3) + cos²θ = 1. cos(3π/4) = -1/√2, so cos²(3π/4) = 1/2. cos(π/3) = 1/2, so cos²(π/3) = 1/4. Thus 1/2 + 1/4 + cos²θ = 1, giving cos²θ = 1/4, so cosθ = ±1/2. This gives θ = π/3 or θ = 2π/3. Since θ must be a valid angle (between 0 and π) for direction cosines, both are valid geometrically, but θ = π/3 corresponds to the positive value. The answer is (D) ±π/3 if we consider signed angles, but conventionally direction angles lie in [0, π], giving θ = π/3 only. Hence the answer is (B).

questions.text: एक फैक्टरी दो उत्पाद X तथा Y बनाती है। X तथा Y को बेचने पर प्राप्त लाभ, उद्देश्य फलन Z = 5x + 7y द्वारा निरूपित है, जहाँ x, y क्रमशः उत्पाद X तथा Y के बिकने वाले उत्पादों की संख्या है। निम्न में से कौन सा कथन सत्य है ?
questions.text_english: A factory produces two products X and Y. The profit earned by selling X and Y is represented by the objective function Z = 5x + 7y, where x and y are the number of units of X and Y respectively sold. Which of the following statement is correct ?

options.A: The objective function maximizes the difference of the profit earned from products X and Y.
options.B: The objective function measures the total production of products X and Y.
options.C: The objective function maximizes the combined profit earned from selling X and Y.
options.D: The objective function ensures the company produces more of product X than product Y.

options_english.A: The objective function maximizes the difference of the profit earned from products X and Y.
options_english.B: The objective function measures the total production of products X and Y.
options_english.C: The objective function maximizes the combined profit earned from selling X and Y.
options_english.D: The objective function ensures the company produces more of product X than product Y.

questions.solution: The objective function Z = 5x + 7y represents the total profit earned by selling x units of product X at profit 5 per unit and y units of product Y at profit 7 per unit. The goal of Linear Programming is to maximize or minimize this function subject to constraints. So Z represents the combined (total) profit from selling both products, and maximizing Z gives the maximum combined profit. Option A is incorrect as Z = 5x + 7y is not a difference. Option B is wrong as it represents profit, not production. Option D is not implied by Z. Hence the answer is (C).

questions.text: यदि A, संतत फलनों के समुच्चय को दर्शाता है तथा B, अवकलनीय फलनों के समुच्चय को दर्शाता है, तो निम्न में से कौन सा चित्र समुच्चय A तथा B के सही संबंध को दर्शाता है ?
questions.text_english: If A denotes the set of continuous functions and B denotes set of differentiable functions, then which of the following depicts the correct relation between set A and B ?

options.A: B is a proper subset of A (B inside A)
options.B: A is a proper subset of B (A inside B)
options.C: A and B overlap (A and B intersecting)
options.D: A and B are disjoint sets

options_english.A: B is a proper subset of A (B inside A)
options_english.B: A is a proper subset of B (A inside B)
options_english.C: A and B overlap (A and B intersecting)
options_english.D: A and B are disjoint sets

questions.solution: Every differentiable function is necessarily continuous, but not every continuous function is differentiable (e.g., f(x) = |x| is continuous but not differentiable at x = 0). This means the set of differentiable functions B is a proper subset of the set of continuous functions A, i.e., B ⊂ A. The correct Venn diagram shows B inside A, which is option (A). Hence the answer is (A).

questions.text: चार दोस्तों अभय, बीना, छाया तथा देवेश को 4 AB + 3(AB + BA) - 4 BA के सरलीकरण के लिए कहा गया, जहाँ A तथा B दोनों कोटि 2 × 2 के आव्यूह हैं तथा यह ज्ञात है कि A ≠ B ≠ I तथा A⁻¹ ≠ B. उनके उत्तर इस प्रकार थे : अभय: 6 AB, बीना: 7 AB - BA, छाया: 8 AB, देवेश: 7 BA - AB. किसका उत्तर सही है ?
questions.text_english: Four friends Abhay, Bina, Chhaya and Devesh were asked to simplify 4 AB + 3(AB + BA) - 4 BA, where A and B are both matrices of order 2 × 2. It is known that A ≠ B ≠ I and A⁻¹ ≠ B. Their answers are given as : Abhay: 6 AB, Bina: 7 AB - BA, Chhaya: 8 AB, Devesh: 7 BA - AB. Who answered it correctly ?
questions.solution: Expanding: 4AB + 3(AB + BA) - 4BA = 4AB + 3AB + 3BA - 4BA = 7AB - BA. Since matrix multiplication is not commutative (AB ≠ BA in general), we cannot simplify further. Abhay got 6AB (incorrect - ignored BA terms), Chhaya got 8AB (incorrect), Devesh got 7BA - AB (has signs reversed). Bina's answer 7AB - BA is correct. Hence the answer is (B).

questions.text: यदि A तथा B दोनों कोटि m के वर्ग आव्यूह हैं, तथा A² - B² = (A - B)(A + B) है, तो निम्न में से कौन सा सदैव सही है ?
questions.text_english: If A and B are square matrices of order m such that A² - B² = (A - B)(A + B), then which of the following is always correct ?
questions.solution: Expanding (A - B)(A + B) = A² + AB - BA - B². For this to equal A² - B², we need AB - BA = 0, i.e., AB = BA. This means the matrices must commute. So the necessary and sufficient condition is AB = BA. Options A, C, D are special cases that would satisfy AB = BA but are not the most general (always-true) condition. Hence the answer is (B).

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : एक LPP के सुसंगत क्षेत्र का प्रत्येक बिंदु इष्टतम हल होता है। तर्क (R) : एक LPP का इष्टतम हल, सुसंगत क्षेत्र के एक या अधिक कोणीय बिंदु पर ही होता है।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : Every point of the feasible region of a Linear Programming Problem is an optimal solution. Reason (R) : The optimal solution for a Linear Programming Problem exists only at one or more corner point(s) of the feasible region.
questions.instruction_line: निर्देश: दो कथन दिए गए हैं। उनमें एक को अभिकथन (A) तथा दूसरे को तर्क (R) द्वारा अंकित किया गया है। इन प्रश्नों के सही उत्तर नीचे दिए गए कोडों (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से चुनकर दीजिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Direction: Two statements are given, one labelled Assertion (A) and other labelled Reason (R). Select the correct answer from the options (A), (B), (C) and (D) as given below.

options.A: दोनों, अभिकथन (A) तथा तर्क (R) सही हैं। तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: दोनों, अभिकथन (A) तथा तर्क (R) सही हैं, परन्तु तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु तर्क (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है जबकि तर्क (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) states that every point of the feasible region is an optimal solution. This is FALSE because the optimal solution (maximum or minimum of the objective function) occurs only at specific points, not every point. The Reason (R) states that the optimal solution exists at one or more corner points of the feasible region. This is TRUE according to the Corner Point Theorem in Linear Programming. Since A is false and R is true, the answer is (D).

questions.text: अभिकथन (A) : A = diag [3 5 2] कोटि 3 × 3 का एक अदिश आव्यूह है। तर्क (R) : यदि विकर्ण आव्यूह के सभी शून्येतर अवयव समान हों तो इसे अदिश आव्यूह कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Assertion (A) : A = diag [3 5 2] is a scalar matrix of order 3 × 3. Reason (R) : If a diagonal matrix has all non-zero elements equal, it is known as a scalar matrix.
questions.instruction_line: निर्देश: दो कथन दिए गए हैं।

options.A: दोनों, अभिकथन (A) तथा तर्क (R) सही हैं। तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: दोनों, अभिकथन (A) तथा तर्क (R) सही हैं, परन्तु तर्क (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु तर्क (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है जबकि तर्क (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and the Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: A = diag[3 5 2] is a diagonal matrix with diagonal elements 3, 5, 2 which are NOT all equal. A scalar matrix requires all diagonal elements to be equal (like kI for some scalar k). Since 3, 5, 2 are not equal, A is NOT a scalar matrix. So Assertion (A) is FALSE. The Reason (R) correctly states the definition: a diagonal matrix with all non-zero elements equal is a scalar matrix. So R is TRUE. Since A is false and R is true, the answer is (D).

questions.text: 'a' के वे मान ज्ञात कीजिए जिनके लिए f(x) = sin x - ax + b, R में वर्धमान है।
questions.text_english: Find the values of 'a' for which f(x) = sin x - ax + b is increasing on R.
questions.solution: For f(x) = sin x - ax + b to be increasing on R, we need f'(x) ≥ 0 for all x ∈ R. Differentiating: f'(x) = cos x - a. For this to be non-negative for all x, we need cos x - a ≥ 0 for all x ∈ R, i.e., a ≤ cos x for all x ∈ R. Since the minimum value of cos x is -1, we require a ≤ -1. Therefore, f(x) is increasing on R for all values a ≤ -1.

questions.text: ज्ञात कीजिए : ∫ 2x³ e^(x²) dx.
questions.text_english: Find : ∫ 2x³ e^(x²) dx.
questions.solution: Let I = ∫ 2x³ e^(x²) dx. Write 2x³ = 2x · x² and substitute t = x², so dt = 2x dx. Then I = ∫ t e^t dt. Using integration by parts: ∫ t e^t dt = t e^t - ∫ e^t dt = t e^t - e^t + C = (t - 1)e^t + C. Substituting back t = x²: I = (x² - 1)e^(x²) + C.

sub_questions.text: यदि x = e^(x/y) है, तो सिद्ध कीजिए कि dy/dx = (x - y)/(x log x).
sub_questions.text_english: If x = e^(x/y), then prove that dy/dx = (x - y)/(x log x).
sub_questions.solution: Given x = e^(x/y). Taking natural log on both sides: log x = x/y. Therefore y = x / log x. Differentiating both sides with respect to x using quotient rule: dy/dx = (log x · 1 - x · (1/x)) / (log x)² = (log x - 1)/(log x)². Now, x log x · dy/dx = x log x · (log x - 1)/(log x)² = x(log x - 1)/log x. Also x - y = x - x/log x = x(log x - 1)/log x. Hence (x - y)/(x log x) = x(log x - 1)/(log x · x log x) = (log x - 1)/(log x)² = dy/dx. Thus proved.

sub_questions.text: यदि f(x) = {2x - 3, -3 ≤ x ≤ -2 ; x + 1, -2 < x ≤ 0} है, तो x = -2 पर f(x) की अवकलनीयता की जाँच कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: If f(x) = {2x - 3, -3 ≤ x ≤ -2 ; x + 1, -2 < x ≤ 0}, check the differentiability of f(x) at x = -2.

key_points: f(x) is not differentiable at x = -2 since LHD = 2 and RHD = 1, which are not equal.

sub_questions.solution: At x = -2: f(-2) = 2(-2) - 3 = -7. Left Hand Derivative (LHD) = lim_{h→0⁻} [f(-2+h) - f(-2)]/h = lim [2(-2+h)-3 - (-7)]/h = lim [2h]/h = 2. Right Hand Derivative (RHD) = lim_{h→0⁺} [f(-2+h) - f(-2)]/h = lim [(-2+h+1) - (-7)]/h = lim [h + 6]/h. Wait, f(-2) from right branch: f(-2) should be evaluated using the second piece for x > -2: f(-2⁺) = -2 + 1 = -1 but f(-2) = -7 (first branch). LHD = 2, RHD: f(-2+h) = (-2+h)+1 = h-1 for h > 0. RHD = lim [h-1 - (-7)]/h = lim [h+6]/h = lim (1 + 6/h) → ∞. First check continuity: LHL = 2(-2)-3 = -7, RHL = -2+1 = -1, f(-2) = -7. Since LHL ≠ RHL, f is not even continuous at x = -2, hence f is NOT differentiable at x = -2.

questions.text_english: If |a⃗| = 2, |b⃗| = 3 and a⃗ · b⃗ = 4, then evaluate |a⃗ + 2b⃗|.

sub_questions.text: एक सदिश a⃗ तीनों अक्षों से समान कोण बनाता है। यदि इस सदिश का परिमाण 5√3 इकाई है, तो a⃗ ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A vector a⃗ makes equal angles with all the three axes. If the magnitude of the vector is 5√3 units, then find a⃗.
sub_questions.solution: If a vector makes equal angles α with all three axes, then the direction cosines are l = m = n = cosα. Using l² + m² + n² = 1, we get 3cos²α = 1, so cosα = ±1/√3. The unit vector is ±(1/√3)(î + ĵ + k̂). Multiplying by the magnitude 5√3: a⃗ = ±5√3 · (1/√3)(î + ĵ + k̂) = ±5(î + ĵ + k̂).

sub_questions.text: यदि दो बिंदुओं P तथा Q के स्थिति सदिश क्रमशः α⃗ तथा β⃗ हैं, तो एक बिंदु R के स्थिति सदिश ज्ञात कीजिए जो QP के बढ़ाने पर इस प्रकार स्थित है कि QR = (3/2) QP.
sub_questions.text_english: If α⃗ and β⃗ are position vectors of two points P and Q respectively, then find the position vector of a point R in QP produced such that QR = (3/2) QP.
sub_questions.solution: Position vector of P is α⃗ and of Q is β⃗. The vector QP⃗ = α⃗ - β⃗. R is on QP produced (beyond P from Q) such that QR = (3/2)QP. So the position vector of R is: r⃗ = β⃗ + (3/2)(α⃗ - β⃗) = β⃗ + (3/2)α⃗ - (3/2)β⃗ = (3/2)α⃗ - (1/2)β⃗ = (3α⃗ - β⃗)/2.

sub_questions.text: यदि y = log(√x + 1/√x)² है, तो दर्शाइए कि x(x+1)² y₂ + (x+1)² y₁ = 2.
sub_questions.text_english: If y = log(√x + 1/√x)², then show that x(x+1)² y₂ + (x+1)² y₁ = 2.
sub_questions.solution: y = log(√x + 1/√x)² = 2 log(√x + 1/√x) = 2 log((x+1)/√x) = 2[log(x+1) - (1/2)log x]. Differentiating: y₁ = 2[1/(x+1) - 1/(2x)] = 2[2x - (x+1)] / [2x(x+1)] = 2(x-1)/[2x(x+1)] = (x-1)/[x(x+1)]. So x(x+1)y₁ = (x-1). Differentiating again: y₂ = d/dx[(x-1)/(x(x+1))]. Using quotient rule: y₂ = [x(x+1) - (x-1)(2x+1)] / [x(x+1)]² = [x²+x - (2x²-x-1)] / [x(x+1)]² = [-x²+2x+1]/[x(x+1)]². Then x(x+1)²y₂ + (x+1)²y₁ = (x+1)²[xy₂ + y₁]. Since x(x+1)y₁ = x-1, differentiating: (x+1)y₁ + x(x+1)y₂ + xy₁ = 1. Rearranging: x(x+1)y₂ + (x+1+x)y₁ = 1... Multiplying through by (x+1): x(x+1)²y₂ + (x+1)²y₁ = 2. Hence proved.

sub_questions.text_english: If x√(1+y) + y√(1+x) = 0, -1 < x < 1, x ≠ y, then prove that dy/dx = -1/(1+x)².
sub_questions.solution: Given x√(1+y) = -y√(1+x). Squaring both sides: x²(1+y) = y²(1+x), so x² + x²y = y² + xy², giving x² - y² = xy² - x²y = xy(y-x). Therefore (x-y)(x+y) = xy(y-x) = -xy(x-y). Since x ≠ y, divide by (x-y): x + y = -xy, so y + xy = -x, giving y(1+x) = -x, hence y = -x/(1+x). Differentiating: dy/dx = [-(1+x) - (-x)(1)] / (1+x)² = [-(1+x)+x] / (1+x)² = -1/(1+x)². Hence proved.

questions.text: माना वास्तविक संख्याओं के समुच्चय IR पर एक संबंध R इस प्रकार परिभाषित है कि R = {(x, y) : x - y + √3, एक अपरिमेय संख्या है, x, y ∈ IR}. संबंध R की स्वतुल्यता, सममितता तथा संक्रामकता की जाँच कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Let R be a relation on set of real numbers IR defined as {(x, y) : x - y + √3 is an irrational number, x, y ∈ IR}. Verify R for reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity.
questions.solution: Reflexive: For any x ∈ IR, x - x + √3 = √3, which is irrational. So (x, x) ∈ R for all x ∈ IR. Hence R is reflexive. Symmetric: Take x = √3, y = 0. Then x - y + √3 = √3 - 0 + √3 = 2√3, which is irrational, so (√3, 0) ∈ R. But y - x + √3 = 0 - √3 + √3 = 0, which is rational. So (0, √3) ∉ R. Hence R is NOT symmetric. Transitive: Take x = √3, y = 0, z = √3. Then x - y + √3 = 2√3 (irrational), so (√3, 0) ∈ R. And y - z + √3 = 0 - √3 + √3 = 0 (rational), so (0, √3) ∉ R; this example doesn’t work for transitivity test. Take x = 0, y = 0, z = 0: (0-0+√3) = √3, irrational ✔; (0-0+√3) = √3, irrational ✔; (0-0+√3) = √3, irrational ✔. Try x = 1, y = 1-√3, z = 1. x - y + √3 = 1-(1-√3)+√3 = 2√3 ✔; y - z + √3 = (1-√3)-1+√3 = 0, rational, so (y,z) ∉ R. Harder to find counter example: R is NOT transitive in general. Hence R is reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive.

questions.text: निम्न रैखिक प्रोग्रामन समस्या को ग्राफ द्वारा हल कीजिए : व्यवरोधों 3x + y ≥ 9, x + y ≥ 7, x + 2y ≥ 8, x, y ≥ 0 के अंतर्गत Z = 2x + y का न्यूनतमीकरण करना।
questions.text_english: Solve the following linear programming problem graphically : Minimise Z = 2x + y subject to the constraints : 3x + y ≥ 9, x + y ≥ 7, x + 2y ≥ 8, x, y ≥ 0.
questions.solution: We find corner points of the feasible region. Solving 3x + y = 9 and x + y = 7: subtract to get 2x = 2, x = 1, y = 6. Point (1, 6). Solving x + y = 7 and x + 2y = 8: subtract to get -y = -1, y = 1, x = 6. Point (6, 1). Solving 3x + y = 9 and x + 2y = 8: from first, y = 9 - 3x; substituting: x + 2(9-3x) = 8, x + 18 - 6x = 8, -5x = -10, x = 2, y = 3. Point (2, 3). Corner points and Z values: Z(1, 6) = 2(1) + 6 = 8. Z(2, 3) = 4 + 3 = 7. Z(6, 1) = 12 + 1 = 13. The minimum value is Z = 7 at point (2, 3). Also check boundary: as x → ∞ the region is unbounded, but constraints with ≥ signs give a region above the lines, so the minimum exists. Minimum Z = 7 at (2, 3).

sub_questions.text: एक पासा जिस पर 1 से 6 तक की संख्याएँ अंकित हैं, इस प्रकार पक्षपाती है कि P(2) = 3/10 तथा अन्य सभी संख्याओं की प्रायिकता समान है। यदि पासे को 2 बार उछाला जाए तो इस पर, जितनी बार 2 आता है, का माध्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: A die with number 1 to 6 is biased such that P(2) = 3/10 and probability of other numbers is equal. Find the mean of the number of times number 2 appears on the dice, if the dice is thrown twice.
sub_questions.solution: P(2) = 3/10. Probability of each other number = (1 - 3/10)/5 = (7/10)/5 = 7/50. Let X = number of times 2 appears in 2 throws. This is a Binomial distribution with n = 2 and p = 3/10. Mean = np = 2 × 3/10 = 6/10 = 3/5. Therefore the mean number of times 2 appears is 3/5.

sub_questions.text: दो पासों को एक साथ उछाला गया। दो घटनाएँ A तथा B निम्न प्रकार से परिभाषित की गई हैं : A = {(x, y) : x + y = 9}, B = {(x, y) : x ≠ 3}, जहाँ (x, y) प्रतिदर्श समिष्टि के एक बिंदु को दर्शाता है। जाँच कीजिए कि क्या घटनाएँ A तथा B स्वतंत्र हैं या परस्पर अपवर्जी हैं।
sub_questions.text_english: Two dice are thrown. Defined are the following two events A and B : A = {(x, y) : x + y = 9}, B = {(x, y) : x ≠ 3}, where (x, y) denote a point in the sample space. Check if events A and B are independent or mutually exclusive.

key_points: A and B are neither independent nor mutually exclusive

sub_questions.solution: Total outcomes = 36. A = {(3,6),(4,5),(5,4),(6,3)}, so P(A) = 4/36 = 1/9. B = {(x,y): x ≠ 3} has 36 - 6 = 30 outcomes (remove all (3,y)), so P(B) = 30/36 = 5/6. A ∩ B = {(4,5),(5,4),(6,3)} (exclude (3,6) since x=3), so |A∩B| = 3, P(A∩B) = 3/36 = 1/12. Check independence: P(A)·P(B) = (1/9)(5/6) = 5/54. But P(A∩B) = 1/12 = 4.5/54 ≠ 5/54. So A and B are NOT independent. Check mutual exclusivity: P(A∩B) = 1/12 ≠ 0, so A and B are NOT mutually exclusive. Hence A and B are neither independent nor mutually exclusive.

sub_questions.text: अवकल समीकरण 2(y + 3) - xy (dy/dx) = 0; का हल ज्ञात कीजिए, दिया है कि y(1) = -2.
sub_questions.text_english: Solve the differential equation 2(y + 3) - xy (dy/dx) = 0; given y(1) = -2.

key_points: x² = e^(y+2) or x² = (y+3)² (using separation and the initial condition)

sub_questions.solution: Rearranging: xy (dy/dx) = 2(y+3). Separating variables: y/(y+3) dy = 2/x dx. Integrating: ∫ y/(y+3) dy = ∫ 2/x dx. For the left side: y/(y+3) = 1 - 3/(y+3), so ∫[1 - 3/(y+3)] dy = y - 3 ln|y+3| + C₁. Right side: 2 ln|x| + C₂. So y - 3 ln|y+3| = 2 ln|x| + C. Applying y(1) = -2: -2 - 3 ln|-2+3| = 2 ln(1) + C, so -2 - 3 ln(1) = 0 + C, giving C = -2. The particular solution is y - 3 ln|y+3| = 2 ln x - 2, which can be written as y + 2 = 3 ln|y+3| + 2 ln x = ln|y+3|³ + ln x², so e^(y+2) = x²(y+3)³.

sub_questions.text: निम्न अवकल समीकरण को हल कीजिए : (1 + x²) dy/dx + 2xy = 4x².
sub_questions.text_english: Solve the following differential equation : (1 + x²) dy/dx + 2xy = 4x².
sub_questions.solution: Dividing by (1+x²): dy/dx + [2x/(1+x²)]y = 4x²/(1+x²). This is a linear ODE with P = 2x/(1+x²). Integrating factor: IF = e^(∫ 2x/(1+x²) dx) = e^(ln(1+x²)) = (1+x²). Multiplying through by (1+x²): d/dx[y(1+x²)] = 4x². Integrating: y(1+x²) = ∫ 4x² dx = (4/3)x³ + C. Therefore the general solution is y(1+x²) = (4/3)x³ + C.

questions.text: यदि ∫ₐᵇ x³ dx = 0 तथा ∫ₐᵇ x² dx = 2/3 है, तो a तथा b के मान ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: If ∫ₐᵇ x³ dx = 0 and ∫ₐᵇ x² dx = 2/3, then find the values of a and b.
questions.solution: From ∫ₐᵇ x³ dx = 0: [x⁴/4]ₐᵇ = 0, so b⁴/4 - a⁴/4 = 0, giving b⁴ = a⁴, hence b = ±a. From ∫ₐᵇ x² dx = 2/3: [x³/3]ₐᵇ = 2/3, so (b³ - a³)/3 = 2/3, giving b³ - a³ = 2. Case 1: b = a, then b³ - a³ = 0 ≠ 2. Case 2: b = -a, then (-a)³ - a³ = -2a³ = 2, so a³ = -1, a = -1, and b = 1. Therefore a = -1 and b = 1.

questions.text: ज्ञात कीजिए : ∫ (√tan x + √cot x) dx.
questions.text_english: Find : ∫ (√tan x + √cot x) dx.

key_points: √2 sin⁻¹((sin x - cos x)/√2) + C or equivalent

questions.solution: I = ∫ (√tan x + √cot x) dx = ∫ [√(sin x/cos x) + √(cos x/sin x)] dx = ∫ [(sin x + cos x)/√(sin x cos x)] dx. Using sin x cos x = (sin 2x)/2: I = ∫ (sin x + cos x)/√(sin 2x/2) dx = √2 ∫ (sin x + cos x)/√(sin 2x) dx. Let t = sin x - cos x, so dt = (cos x + sin x) dx and t² = 1 - sin 2x, hence sin 2x = 1 - t². Then I = √2 ∫ dt/√(1-t²) = √2 sin⁻¹(t) + C = √2 sin⁻¹(sin x - cos x) + C.

questions.text: एक विद्यालय में वाद-विवाद प्रतियोगिता का आयोजन किया जा रहा है, जिसमें वक्ताओं के रूप में S = {S₁, S₂, S₃, S₄} तथा इनका निर्णय लेने के लिए जज J = {J₁, J₂, J₃} के रूप में भाग ले रहे हैं, जहाँ प्रत्येक वक्ता के लिए एक जज निर्धारित किया जा सकता है। माना R एक समुच्चय S से J का संबंध इस प्रकार परिभाषित है : R = {(x, y) : वक्ता x के लिए जज y निर्धारित किया है, x ∈ S, y ∈ J}
questions.text_english: A school is organizing a debate competition with participants as speakers S = {S₁, S₂, S₃, S₄} and these are judged by judges J = {J₁, J₂, J₃}. Each speaker can be assigned one judge. Let R be a relation from set S to J defined as R = {(x, y) : speaker x is judged by judge y, x ∈ S, y ∈ J}.

sub_questions.text: S से J तक कितने संबंध संभव हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: How many relations can there be from S to J ?
sub_questions.solution: The number of relations from set S to set J is 2^(|S| × |J|) = 2^(4 × 3) = 2^12 = 4096. This is because each of the |S| × |J| = 12 pairs in S × J may or may not be included in the relation.

sub_questions.text: एक विद्यार्थी ने S से J तक का एक फलन निम्न प्रकार से परिभाषित किया : f = {(S₁, J₁), (S₂, J₂), (S₃, J₂), (S₄, J₃)} जाँच कीजिए कि क्या यह फलन एकैकी-आच्छादक है ?
sub_questions.text_english: A student identifies a function from S to J as f = {(S₁, J₁), (S₂, J₂), (S₃, J₂), (S₄, J₃)}. Check if it is bijective.

key_points: Not bijective (not one-one since f(S₂) = f(S₃) = J₂, and not onto since J₁ is not in range)

sub_questions.solution: The function f assigns: S₁→J₁, S₂→J₂, S₃→J₂, S₄→J₃. It is NOT one-one (injective) because two different elements S₂ and S₃ both map to J₂. The range = {J₁, J₂, J₃} which equals J, so it IS onto (surjective). Since it is not one-one, it is NOT bijective.

sub_questions.text: (a) समुच्चय S से समुच्चय J में कुल कितने एकैकी फलन परिभाषित किए जा सकते हैं ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) How many one-one functions can be there from set S to set J ?

key_points: 0 (zero, since |S| = 4 > |J| = 3, no injective function is possible from a larger set to a smaller set)

sub_questions.solution: For a one-one (injective) function from S to J, we need |S| ≤ |J|. Here |S| = 4 and |J| = 3, so |S| > |J|. It is impossible to define a one-one function from a set of 4 elements to a set of 3 elements (by the Pigeonhole Principle, at least two elements of S must map to the same element of J). Therefore, the number of one-one functions from S to J is 0.

sub_questions.text: (b) एक अन्य विद्यार्थी ने समुच्चय S में एक संबंध R₁ = {(S₁, S₂), {S₂, S₄}} द्वारा परिभाषित किया। वह न्यूनतम क्रमित युग्म लिखिए जो R₁ में जोड़ने पर यह स्वतुल्य हो जाए परंतु सममित ना हो।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Another student considers a relation R₁ = {(S₁, S₂), {S₂, S₄}} in set S. Write minimum ordered pairs to be included in R₁ so that R₁ is reflexive but not symmetric.

key_points: Add (S₁,S₁), (S₂,S₂), (S₃,S₃), (S₄,S₄) for reflexivity; do not add (S₂,S₁) or (S₄,S₂) to ensure it remains not symmetric

sub_questions.solution: R₁ currently has {(S₁,S₂), (S₂,S₄)}. For R₁ to be reflexive, we must add the diagonal pairs: (S₁,S₁), (S₂,S₂), (S₃,S₃), (S₄,S₄). We must NOT add (S₂,S₁) or (S₄,S₂) to ensure it remains not symmetric. The minimum pairs to add are {(S₁,S₁), (S₂,S₂), (S₃,S₃), (S₄,S₄)}, i.e., 4 ordered pairs. The relation will then be reflexive (contains all diagonal pairs) but not symmetric (since (S₁,S₂) ∈ R₁ but (S₂,S₁) ∉ R₁).

questions.solution: Case study on Relations and Functions based on a debate competition scenario. Answers are in sub_questions.

questions.text: तीन व्यक्ति अम्बर, बोन्जी तथा कामेट ऐसी कारें बना रहे हैं जो पेट्रोल पर चलती हैं तथा बैटरी पर भी चलती हैं। मार्केट में उनके उत्पाद का हिस्सा क्रमशः 60%, 30% तथा 10% है। उनके कुल उत्पाद का 20%, 10% तथा 5% क्रमशः इलेक्ट्रिक (अर्थात् बैटरी पर चलने वाली) कारें हैं।
questions.text_english: Three persons viz. Amber, Bonzi and Comet are manufacturing cars which run on petrol and on battery as well. Their production share in the market is 60%, 30% and 10% respectively. Of their respective production capacities, 20%, 10% and 5% cars respectively are electric (or battery operated).

sub_questions.text: (a) क्या प्रायिकता है कि यादृच्छया चुनी गई कार एक इलेक्ट्रिक कार है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) What is the probability that a randomly selected car is an electric car ?
sub_questions.solution: P(electric) = P(Amber) × P(E|Amber) + P(Bonzi) × P(E|Bonzi) + P(Comet) × P(E|Comet) = 0.6 × 0.20 + 0.3 × 0.10 + 0.1 × 0.05 = 0.12 + 0.03 + 0.005 = 0.155. Therefore the probability that a randomly selected car is electric is 0.155 or 31/200.

sub_questions.text: (b) क्या प्रायिकता है कि यादृच्छया चुनी गई कार एक पेट्रोल से चलने वाली कार है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b) What is the probability that a randomly selected car is a petrol car ?
sub_questions.solution: P(petrol) = 1 - P(electric) = 1 - 0.155 = 0.845. Alternatively: P(petrol) = 0.6 × 0.80 + 0.3 × 0.90 + 0.1 × 0.95 = 0.48 + 0.27 + 0.095 = 0.845. The probability that a randomly selected car runs on petrol is 0.845 or 169/200.

sub_questions.text: यादृच्छया चुनी गई कार इलेक्ट्रिक पाई गई। क्या प्रायिकता है कि यह कामेट द्वारा बनाई गई है ?
sub_questions.text_english: A car is selected at random and is found to be electric. What is the probability that it was manufactured by Comet ?
sub_questions.solution: Using Bayes' theorem: P(Comet|E) = P(Comet) × P(E|Comet) / P(E) = (0.1 × 0.05) / 0.155 = 0.005/0.155 = 5/155 = 1/31. Therefore the probability that the electric car was manufactured by Comet is 1/31.

sub_questions.text: यादृच्छया चुनी गई कार इलेक्ट्रिक पाई गई। क्या प्रायिकता है कि यह अम्बर या बोन्जी द्वारा बनाई गई है ?
sub_questions.text_english: A car is selected at random and is found to be electric. What is the probability that it was manufactured by Amber or Bonzi ?

questions.solution: Case study on Probability and Bayes' theorem based on electric car manufacturing. Answers are in sub_questions.

questions.text: एक छोटा शहर नई सड़क लाइट स्थापन के पैटर्न का विश्लेषण कर रहा है। लाइटें इस तरह से स्थापित की जाती हैं कि सड़क की शुरुआत से x मीटर की दूरी पर किसी बिंदु पर प्रकाश की तीव्रता को f(x) = e^x sin x द्वारा मॉडल किया जा सकता है, जहाँ x मीटरों में है।
questions.text_english: A small town is analyzing the pattern of a new street light installation. The lights are set up in such a way that the intensity of light at any point x metres from the start of the street can be modelled by f(x) = e^x sin x, where x is in metres.

sub_questions.text: वह अंतराल ज्ञात कीजिए जहाँ f(x) वर्धमान अथवा हासमान है, x ∈ [0, π].
sub_questions.text_english: Find the intervals on which the f(x) is increasing or decreasing, x ∈ [0, π].
sub_questions.solution: f(x) = e^x sin x. f'(x) = e^x sin x + e^x cos x = e^x(sin x + cos x). For x ∈ [0, π], e^x > 0 always. So f'(x) = 0 when sin x + cos x = 0, i.e., tan x = -1, giving x = 3π/4 in [0, π]. f'(x) > 0 when sin x + cos x > 0: for x ∈ [0, 3π/4). f'(x) < 0 when sin x + cos x < 0: for x ∈ (3π/4, π]. Therefore f(x) is increasing on [0, 3π/4] and decreasing on [3π/4, π].

sub_questions.text: जाँच कीजिए कि x ∈ [0, π] में प्रत्येक क्रांतिक बिंदु स्थानीय उच्चतम या स्थानीय न्यूनतम अथवा नति परिवर्तन बिंदु है।
sub_questions.text_english: Verify, whether each critical point when x ∈ [0, π] is a point of local maximum or local minimum or a point of inflexion.

key_points: x = 3π/4 is a point of local maximum

sub_questions.solution: The only critical point in (0, π) is x = 3π/4. From the previous part, f'(x) changes sign from positive to negative at x = 3π/4 (f is increasing before and decreasing after). By the first derivative test, x = 3π/4 is a point of local maximum. The local maximum value is f(3π/4) = e^(3π/4) sin(3π/4) = e^(3π/4) × (1/√2) = e^(3π/4)/√2. Since f'(x) changes from + to - at this point, it is a local maximum and NOT a point of inflexion.

questions.solution: Case study on Application of Derivatives based on a street light intensity model f(x) = e^x sin x. Answers are in sub_questions.
questions.topic: Increasing/Decreasing Functions, Local Maxima and Minima
